Subject: Production: sudden surge in 5xx / 429 / timeouts - urgent

Irene — we’re seeing a rapid degradation in calls to Redwood from our production payment flow starting ~08:15 PST. Symptoms: widespread 429s, intermittent 5xx, and a bunch of client-side timeouts. P99 latency has spiked from ~420ms to >3.5s. This is impacting checkouts (failed auths / retries).

We’ve attached a sample of failed request payloads and a p99 chart. Can you confirm whether this is a runtime issue on your side or something in the model path? We need an ETA and immediate mitigation steps — customers are already seeing failed transactions.

Thanks,
Maya Patel

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>

Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Production: sudden surge in 5xx / 429 / timeouts - urgent

Team — initial findings from the runtime trace:
- At ~08:14 PST we saw a sudden traffic spike from a small set of ZenFlow IPs that triggered aggressive caching churn on the KV cache. Cache misses + loading led to CPU contention on the serving pods.
- Autoscaler lag: scale-up actions were queued but not applied fast enough due to instance boot contention in us-west.
- Result: request queueing -> client timeouts -> client retries -> retry amplification -> sustained high 429 and 5xx.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (ordered):
1) Rate-limit (token-bucket) on the affected route for ZenFlow to cap concurrency at current steady-state + 20% while we stabilize.
2) Push header to clients to disable auto-retry: X-RW-Client-Retry: disabled (we’ll coordinate a transient SDK flag).
3) Temporary autoscaler override: force +3 instances in the dedicated pool serving redact-v2-6b in us-west.
4) Apply a hotfix that pins the KV eviction window to reduce thrash (runtime patch INF-5873).

ETA: token-bucket + header toggle: 15–25 minutes. Autoscaler override + hotfix rollout: 60–90 minutes (hotfix requires canary then fast rollback option).

I’ve created PD: #pagerduty_xyz123 and JIRA INF-5873 (see links). I’ll start the rate-limit and header work now.

— Sean Gallagher
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
